story.title: Story 1: Project Artifact Association Without Process Ownership

result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 1 focused on the in-scope read-model alignment: project-shell artifact summaries, process current-material projection, referenced-artifact reviewability, and the story’s mapped tests/gates across Convex, server, and client surfaces.
mockOrShimAuditFindings: No production-path mocks, shims, or fake adapters were introduced in the reviewed Story 1 surfaces. The only fakes observed were test-only harnesses such as `InMemoryPlatformStore` and fake Convex contexts under `tests/` and `convex/*.test.ts`.
additionalObservations: Story 1’s read paths are aligned to project-scoped artifact summaries and process-local current refs: `artifactSummarySchema` now exposes only `artifactId`, `displayName`, `currentVersionLabel`, and `updatedAt`, the project-shell UI no longer renders ownership copy, `setCurrentProcessMaterialRefs` updates per-process current refs after same-project validation, `MaterialsSectionReader` filters artifacts by those refs, and `DefaultArtifactReviewService` allows review when the process currently references the artifact while preserving earlier-version provenance via `producedByProcessId`.

Legacy ownership residue still exists in the out-of-scope durable write path: `convex/artifacts.ts` keeps `artifacts.processId` in the table shape and still patches it during checkpoint writes. I did not treat that as a Story 1 failure because the story explicitly scopes revision/write-path realignment to later work, and none of the reviewed Story 1 read paths rely on that field anymore.
Repo validation remains consistent with the onboarding baseline: `guard:no-test-changes` is a scaffolded skip inside `green-verify`, and `test:e2e` is still a scaffolded skip inside `verify-all`.
